_doc: MIG-021v3 V3-§1 — Cataloger rules registry. Declarative encoding of Architect §4 — the five rules every cataloger consults. Catalogers reference rules by ID via cece::rules::rule(RuleId::X). New rules can be added without touching Rust code; existing rules can be refined by editing this file. Schema is versioned implicitly by the RuleId enum in src/cece/rules.rs — adding a rule here AND a variant there keeps them in sync (the loader asserts presence on first call).

rules.name: Rule of Authority
rules.description: Frontmatter > body text > AI-inferred. The User-Authority Cataloger encodes this absolutely: when frontmatter has explicit values, no other cataloger overrides them. Other catalogers respect it implicitly — they never voice an opinion that contradicts an explicit frontmatter value.

rules.name: Rule of Application
rules.description: Classify by what the note USES the concept for, not what it merely mentions. A note saying 'al-Bukhari is the source of many authentic hadiths' is about al-Bukhari (the who); a note saying 'حدثنا الإمام البخاري في صحيحه أن النبي ﷺ قال...' is testimony/scriptural transmitting al-Bukhari's content (the use). Linguistic and Structural Catalogers must distinguish use from mention; the Reasoning Cataloger should be primed for this.

rules.name: Rule of Three
rules.description: When 3+ candidates have similar weight at a depth, ascend one level and assign the parent rather than guess at the leaf. Encoded in each cataloger's 'self_reported_confidence: low + descend_uncertain: true' path. Mirrors 'abstain at depth' from the paper §3.4.

rules.name: Rule of Side-channel Preference
rules.description: When prose evidence and side-channel evidence disagree, prefer the side-channel. Side channels (Living Links typed neighbors, CAE morphology, Lexical Bridge equivalents) are harder to fake than prose mentions. The Linguistic and Graph Catalogers encode this directly; synthesis weighting reinforces it.

rules.name: Rule of Authority Control
rules.description: When neighboring notes (via Living Links) have a consensus classification and the current note is in their semantic neighborhood, prefer to align with them unless explicit reason otherwise. Mirrors LCSH authority files — the cataloger consults what similar items were classified as. Encoded in the Graph Cataloger.
